lines.en: My heart sank the moment I felt for a pulse on Han Sooyoung’s cold body.
I was more surprised by my own shock than by the fact that Han Sooyoung was dead.
A short while later, I began to think clearly again, little by little.
“······Dokja-ssi?”
Yoo Sangah got up too, as though she had noticed something.
With Yoo Sangah’s help, I examined Han Sooyoung’s corpse.
“There are no wounds.”
The situation became a complete mystery.
No wounds. Then was it poison?
The only poison capable of killing Han Sooyoung without leaving any signs of poisoning was Formless Poison.
But there was no way a poison like that was available yet.
That wasn’t the only question.
If someone had used poison, why were the rest of us unharmed?
Even if someone possessed such a poison, there was no reason to single out Han Sooyoung for poisoning.
For that matter, it was strange that I had suddenly fallen asleep.
······Wait. Fallen asleep?
“Ugh······ Sorry. I slept too much, didn’t I?”
I could see Shin Yoosung groggily opening her eyes.
I suddenly turned to Yoo Sangah.
“Yoo Sangah-ssi, were you asleep the whole time too?”

Yoo Sangah blushed as though embarrassed. If she hadn’t woken up either, that meant none of us had kept watch last night. In other words, once I, the last person on watch, had fallen asleep, everyone had been asleep.
I was an idiot.
My suspicions should have begun with ‘Why did I fall asleep?’ rather than ‘Who killed Han Sooyoung, and how?’
Sleep magic?
No. Returnees were the ones who liked using magic like that.
Pressure-point strikes?
Even if someone used them, they would have to evade my senses.
That left only one answer.
As I approached the campfire, I saw the scattered bones of the groll we had eaten yesterday.
If the entire group had fallen asleep, this was the most likely explanation.
When I cleared away the pile of bones we had picked clean, I noticed loose green powder on the ground.
‘Yanaspreta stems.’
Just as I thought. Nothing else could have caused this. Someone had mixed powdered stems into the groll meat. Yanaspreta stems induced a powerful sleep effect unless consumed with their sap.
An otherworldly ingredient, a plant whose poison even [Donguibogam] couldn’t protect against. That was why we had always boiled it together with the slime······.
“Who cooked the groll yesterday?”
“I think it was Sooyoung-ssi······.”
I let out a small sigh.
What we had eaten yesterday was the meat of the young groll Shin Yoosung had failed to tame. And the person who had killed that young groll was none other than Han Sooyoung.
“She got us.”
I approached Han Sooyoung’s pale corpse.
I had been so flustered that I had briefly forgotten.
An avatar wouldn’t disappear unless its head burst.
But why had she pulled a stunt like this?
She was bound by the ‘Temporary Pledge’ anyway, so she couldn’t run away.
Just then, blue light rose from the area around Han Sooyoung’s heart.
“One moment.”
Ignoring the others’ reactions, I stomped on Han Sooyoung’s head. Blue light burst out, and the avatar vanished.
[The avatar of character ‘Han Sooyoung’ is receiving the effects of the contract violation in her place.]
[Character ‘Han Sooyoung’ sacrifices her avatar to offset most of the penalty from the ‘Temporary Pledge’.]
Yoo Sangah let out a groan, as though she finally understood.
I hadn’t known an avatar could do this either.
I had seen them take damage in place of the original body in the ‘original novel,’ but I had never imagined they could pay the price of a contract too.
The word ‘most’ suggested the penalty hadn’t been completely offset, but her original body probably hadn’t died.
Shin Yoosung asked.
“Has that unnie left?”
“Looks like it.”
There was no point asking why.
Thinking about it, Han Sooyoung had little to gain by traveling with me.
―My constellation donations have already dropped lately from hanging around with you.
I would soon meet up with the others from Chungmuro, and they would be no less hostile toward Han Sooyoung than Yoo Sangah was.
―Tch. How’s someone supposed to live with the misery of never being trusted?
Han Sooyoung would be alone, surrounded by enemies. Perhaps, however briefly, I had deluded myself into thinking she could become one of us.
A few coins and a single note lay where the avatar had scattered into pure white powder.
―For the food
A farewell so very like her.
As though wiping out all the time we had spent together, her avatar drifted away in the breeze from the Han River.
What I did wonder was why Han Sooyoung had stayed with me until now, even though she could use an avatar for [Proxy Death]······.
I didn’t know.
Just as I couldn’t read Yoo Sangah’s mind, I couldn’t read Han Sooyoung’s either.
Even ‘Ways of Survival,’ which explained everything, didn’t tell me things like this.
“Let’s get moving too.”
Just then, a strange sensation came over me with a tingling jolt.
Omniscient Reader’s Viewpoint?
I instinctively looked in the direction the feeling had come from, but there was nothing in particular to see.
········Was I imagining it?
“Idiot.”
Han Sooyoung spoke as she looked toward the abandoned building from atop a distant high-rise. The breeze from the Han River seeping through her ripped jeans was cold. Biting her lip, she muttered.
“······Seriously, shouldn’t you at least pretend to look for me?”
Even as she said it, she knew he couldn’t actually do that.
It was probably only natural.
After all, he, too, was probably every bit as much a ‘reader’ as she was.
She opened her notepad and began writing something down.
It was a habit she couldn’t help as a writer: whenever inspiration struck, she had to write it down.
「Being good at reading books doesn’t necessarily mean being good at understanding people.」
‘We’ll meet again soon.’
She didn’t know what ending Kim Dokja wanted.
But as long as they moved toward the ending, they were certain to meet.
「Even she couldn’t know whether they would be enemies or allies the next time they met.」
Han Sooyoung closed her smartphone and walked down the road.
The morning flew by.

That afternoon, Shin Yoosung’s Magic Power and Agility reached the scenario limit of 60. Feeling it was about time, I bought a [Behind the Scenes Contract] from Bihyung. He grumbled but handed me the contract.
[······You know doing this won’t change the ‘disaster,’ right?]

[That kid’s present isn’t ‘directly connected’ to the future disaster. The disaster comes from a universe that branched off from the first worldline. Even if their existence is connected, their history······.]
‘Cut the useless chatter and give me the contract.’
Once I finished filling out the contract, I handed it to Shin Yoosung.
“I don’t have any stigmas right now, and I can’t lend you power like the other constellations. But I do have quite a lot of coins.”
“You don’t have to sign if you don’t want to. But if you sign with me, you definitely won’t regret it.”
“Mom told me not to sign things like this carelessly······.”
“It’s all right. I’m not really going to act as a constellation sponsor.”
“If I sign this, does that mean I can’t sign with another constellation?”
“Yes.”
Shin Yoosung hesitated for a moment, then nodded as though she had made up her mind.
“All right. I’ve decided to trust you anyway, ajusshi.”
[The ‘Behind the Scenes Contract’ has been concluded.]
[You have become the sponsor of incarnation ‘Shin Yoosung.’]
Dazzling radiance rose around Shin Yoosung and me. But unlike the splendid rays of light, the message that appeared was paltry.
[You are not a constellation. Most constellation sponsor privileges are unavailable.]
<List of Available Privileges>
[1. Incarnation Sponsorship]
[2. Incarnation Encouragement]
Well, I had expected that.
This was probably all I could do for now.
[The constellation ‘Prisoner of the Golden Headband’ snorts.]
[The constellation ‘Secretive Plotter’ congratulates you on your first contract.]
[You have received a donation of 5000 coins.]
[A considerable number of constellations wish to become your constellation sponsor.]
The constellations’ response was enthusiastic too.
This was different again from the time with Gong Pildu of the Ten Evils.
Shin Yoosung would now be my direct incarnation.
So the constellations in the ‘incarnation-seeking’ camp couldn’t help getting excited about me.
I was an ‘incarnation’ with an ‘incarnation’ of my own, even though I wasn’t a constellation yet.

Thus, any constellation that signed with me would naturally gain Shin Yoosung under its command too. The more incarnations I acquired this way, the more rapidly the number of constellations who wanted me would rise.
[The channel’s going to explode······!]
Leaving Bihyung to his delighted screams, I turned to the others and spoke.
“I think it’s about time we set off. Let’s cross the Han River.”
“But we still haven’t found a bridge. Will we be all right?”
“We’ll swim.”
“Pardon?”
“You know how, right?”
Yoo Sangah looked back and forth between me and the Han River with a worried expression.
I could guess what she was worried about.
The Han River’s water level had risen still higher. Within it, even more ichthyosaurs than yesterday were roaring intermittently. Each one was grade 7. Shin Yoosung spoke.
“I can’t swim······.”
“Hold on to this while we cross.”
I held out a Styrofoam box I had found beforehand. I asked Yoo Sangah to connect the box to me with [Arachne’s Web].
“Let’s go.”
When I jumped into the Han River without hesitation, Yoo Sangah immediately followed. Shin Yoosung seemed a little frightened, but she soon grabbed the Styrofoam and dipped her feet into the river.
The cold water of the Han River enveloped my body. The fishy smell of unfamiliar monsters. The ichthyosaurs’ movements began to change. Yoo Sangah asked.
―Will we really be all right?
Of course we wouldn’t.
But considering the time we had left, this was the surest method.
―We’ll get out immediately if it becomes truly dangerous.
―······All right.
―So before it becomes truly dangerous, act as though it already is.
―Pardon?
―Only then will Yoosung awaken quickly. Stage a crisis on purpose. Understood?
I began swimming toward the middle of the Han River, towing the Styrofoam.
There was a reason I had told Shin Yoosung not to worry and simply raise her skill levels.
It didn’t appear in her Attributes Window, but she had an innate ability to adapt and think on her feet.
An ordinary little girl could never survive all the way to the fifth scenario.
She might seem like nothing more than a good kid, but Shin Yoosung wasn’t that simple inside.

A child who killed her pet dog in a crisis, deceived adults, and disguised herself to win the favor of the strong. That was the kind of child Shin Yoosung was. From the moment she first met us, all sorts of calculations had probably been running through her head.
I spoke to Shin Yoosung, who was already gauging the situation.
“Yoosung.”
“Y-yes!”
“Don’t run away.”
“If you run away here, you’ll never be able to go back.”
Shin Yoosung’s slightly parted lips closed.
Shin Yoosung was a clever child rather than a crafty one.
“Do what you can.”
Cheap tricks wouldn’t work.
There was no one to protect her simply because she was a child.
“······All right.”
Fear into terror, and terror soon into resolve.
[Character ‘Shin Yoosung’ activates ‘Advanced Diverse Communication Lv.3’!]
Killing intent surged around us. I could sense more and more predators stalking their prey.
Ten were visible above the surface alone.
Too many to deal with at once. But we could escape if we wanted to. Once we were out of the Han River, the ichthyosaurs couldn’t follow us.
“Dokja-ssi!”
Yoo Sangah’s warning cry. The ichthyosaurs had begun their attack.
Sharp ichthyosaur fangs came at us from every direction at once.
[‘Blade of Faith’ is activated.]
I swung my blade and immediately pierced one ichthyosaur’s maw. The bodies of those that missed slammed against the water.
Kraaash!

The ichthyosaurs’ twisting bodies churned up the Han River. I flew through the air with the spraying river water. When I looked back, Shin Yoosung had lost her grip on the Styrofoam and was rising into the air.
A rush of wind swept through the sky, and Yoo Sangah sent a spiderweb toward Shin Yoosung.
A combination of [Hermes Walking Method] and [Arachne’s Web].
While Yoo Sangah caught Shin Yoosung safely, I used a dead ichthyosaur as a foothold and began swinging my sword at the approaching ichthyosaurs.
“Over here, you bastards!”

Ten or so ichthyosaurs cut through the current toward me. The river surged like a giant wave, and the ichthyosaur corpse beneath my feet rocked precariously. I steadied my breathing and adjusted my stance.
Using [Way of the Wind] would let me get out of this crisis easily, but that wouldn’t look desperate enough.
“Ajusshi!”

Shin Yoosung’s expression grew frantic in Yoo Sangah’s arms. Several fangs dug into my skin, and I swung my sword again and again. A few ichthyosaurs fell away with fatal wounds, but their numbers didn’t diminish. The blood flowing down my body quickly chilled, and breathing grew harder and harder. But I smiled.
Get more frantic.
Want it more.
Get more desperate.
You have to.
Fshshshsh!
An ichthyosaur’s fang left a hideous wound where it grazed me.
Blood began pouring from the ragged flesh.
A message rang in my ears, almost splitting my eardrums.
[The attribute evolution of character ‘Shin Yoosung’ is imminent.]
[Incarnation ‘Shin Yoosung’ enters a trance state.]
Shin Yoosung’s eyes were turning white. She looked just like Lee Gilyoung when he gave it his all. Exactly as I had imagined. All of this had been staged to bring Shin Yoosung to this moment.
[Character ‘Shin Yoosung’ activates ‘Taming Lv.9’!]
Her level 60 Magic Power poured out an aura like a waterfall and began spreading along the Han River’s currents.
Rrrrrumble.
The charging ichthyosaurs faltered. As though responding to a vast mind, they shuddered and moaned.
Kiiiiii······?
The number of ichthyosaurs visible above the surface increased further.
There had been about ten before, but now there were well over twenty. That meant, counting those underwater, at least twice that many ichthyosaurs were gathering around us.
But soon the ichthyosaurs turned toward me again.
The confused ichthyosaurs exuded an even sharper menace, their killing intent growing still more savage.
Kiaaaaaaa!
Damn it, had it failed?
“Yoo Sangah-ssi!”
There was no choice. Our best option now was to use her stigma to get away quickly. Yoo Sangah nodded and approached, sending out threads and evading the ichthyosaurs. I called to Shin Yoosung.
“Yoosung. You can stop now. Shin Yoosung!”
But Shin Yoosung didn’t answer.
The waves of energy rising around Shin Yoosung grew stronger, until her body was completely enveloped in a blue aura.
That was when a whirlpool formed in the middle of the Han River.
Rrrrrumble.
The current swept me away before I could do anything. The ichthyosaurs around me collided with one another and screamed. Barely clinging to an ichthyosaur’s scales, I endured the centrifugal force.
And the next moment.

A huge spray of water shot up, and an ichthyosaur that looked five or six times the size of the others slowly rose. It was so enormous that I hadn’t thought it could really be an ichthyosaur. It was even bigger than the sea commander I had killed.
Majestic whiskers. The aloof gaze of a ruler over an entire species.
Every ichthyosaur around it was bowing its head to the water’s surface.
[Grade 5 marine species (海水種), ‘Queen Mirabad,’ has appeared!]
······Damn it. Of all things, had she called this one?
I had known Shin Yoosung was gifted, but I hadn’t imagined she was talented enough to call a ‘Queen.’
A monster species on par with a lesser disaster.
As I opened [Bookmark] to activate [Way of the Wind], I heard Yoo Sangah’s voice.
“······Dokja-ssi?”
When I turned, Shin Yoosung was floating in the air.

Following the path of aura extending toward Queen Mirabad, Shin Yoosung slowly approached the Queen’s body. The Queen looked at Shin Yoosung, and Shin Yoosung looked at the Queen. Shin Yoosung’s little hand quietly stroked the bridge of the Queen’s nose.
The currents around us subsided, and the ichthyosaurs above the surface quietly disappeared.
When I looked back again, Shin Yoosung was riding on the Queen’s head.
Once again, I realized just what kind of being Shin Yoosung was.
Beast Lord.
Ruler of all monsters.
Shin Yoosung was looking at me as the color slowly returned to her eyes.
She wiped away her nosebleed as though it were nothing and spoke.
“Let’s go, ajusshi.”
I nodded.

I remembered Department Head Han Myungoh once boasting that he had bought a private yacht for his vacation home in the Maldives. What had he said? That the moment the propeller cut through the water, it felt like a highway had opened up across the sea?
Shwaaaaa!
I knew exactly what that felt like now.
If the sea Department Head Han had traveled was something like the Gyeongbu Expressway, I felt as though I was on the Autobahn now.
“······This really is incredible.”

Riding on the rear of the Queen, Yoo Sangah and I stared spellbound at the parting waters of the Han River. As though testing her control over the Queen, Shin Yoosung didn’t head straight across, but cut through the water leading a shoal of ichthyosaurs. Now that the Han River had become a safe zone, we might as well head for a stretch of shore near Yongsan District.
Grooooo.
Like ducklings following their mother, the ichthyosaurs responded to Queen Mirabad and swam in formation.
I closed my eyes, feeling the cool air batter my face.
This felt really fantastic.
A luxury I could never have enjoyed if the world had stayed as it was.
Shin Yoosung stayed on the Queen’s head, synchronizing with its mind and continually muttering something.
Watching her, Yoo Sangah spoke in a voice filled with mixed feelings.
“But Dokja-ssi, if Yoosung gets stronger now, won’t the Yoosung coming from the future get stronger too?”
Just as I had expected. I had thought she would ask that.
“That won’t happen.”
If things followed the original novel, the disaster coming this time was Shin Yoosung from ‘the future of another round.’
The Shin Yoosung who had been betrayed by Yoo Joonghyuk and abandoned outside the worldlines.

After losing her own branch of time and wandering the universe, she became part of a scenario through the Star Stream’s blessing. Then she descended into a scenario of a past round as a ‘disaster.’ Yoo Sangah raised a question.
“Then even if the present Yoosung dies, wouldn’t the future disaster stay alive? Their branches are completely different······.”
“Have you heard of ‘Disconnected Film Theory’?”
I spoke as I watched the current split in two.
“Put simply, it works like this. Let’s suppose Yoosung’s history, beginning from a single worldline, is one strip of ‘film.’”
“Film······ You mean movie film?”
I nodded and spoke.
“If we call this worldline we’re in ‘film number 1,’ then there must be countless other films in other worldlines, right? There would be film number 2, and, well, film number 34 too.”
“Yes. I suppose so?”

“But what would happen if one of those films had its beginning cut off and was attached to the end of film number 1? Say only the latter part of the torn film number 34 was stuck onto the end of film number 1. What do you think would happen if you played that film?”
Yoo Sangah seemed to ponder for a moment.
“Then the footage would change partway through······ Oh, wait. So the two stories can’t affect each other······?”
“Exactly.”

“Ah······ So that’s the situation Yoosung is in now. The Yoosung in film number 1 is the present one, and the Yoosung in film number 34 is the disaster. But because the two stories exist completely independently, even if the Yoosung in our world changes, she can’t affect the disaster······.”
Yoo Sangah really was smart.
“But that still doesn’t answer my question. Then even if the present Yoosung dies, shouldn’t the disaster remain?”
“The contents of the two tapes can’t affect each other, but the tapes themselves are ‘connected.’”
“Pardon?”
“What would happen if the tape at the front caught fire?”
Yoo Sangah gave a small exclamation.
“The tape at the back······ would burn too.”
Because the two worldlines had been forcibly connected, if the present Shin Yoosung died, the future Shin Yoosung would die too.
But a change in the present Shin Yoosung wouldn’t suddenly change the future Shin Yoosung. That ambiguous paradox was the crux of this disaster.
“You really know a lot, Dokja-ssi. I’ve heard of parallel universe theory, but I’ve never heard of a theory like that.”
I nodded awkwardly.
Of course she hadn’t.
Because this was a theory invented by the author of ‘Ways of Survival.’
As I’d said time and again, Ways of Survival hadn’t flopped for nothing.
Wooooo.
A little later, a soft sound marked our stop, and the Han River’s currents grew calm.
We had finally reached the other side of the Han River. After setting us down on the ground, the Queen disappeared back into the river.
Only then, as though her tension had eased, Shin Yoosung let out a sigh deep enough to sink the ground.
“······How did I do?”
“You did great. Good work.”
“Okay.”
Shin Yoosung’s face was curiously flushed.
She seemed to like being praised.
There was no one left to praise this child now, after all.
That was when I sensed fierce hostility from among the forest of buildings in Yongsan District.
Thud. Thud.
An enormous shadow seemed to approach through the forest of buildings, then a huge green scythe appeared between them.
······A giant praying mantis?
Boys riding atop a monster of the insect king species were looking down at me.
“Dokja-hyung?”
Lee Gilyoung in a crooked snapback, and Han Donghoon wearing headphones.
Lee Gilyoung slid down the mantis’s body and ran straight into my arms.
His snapback came off, letting me feel his bristly hair.
It had been exactly a week since we’d last seen each other.
My smartphone buzzed and received a message. It was from Han Donghoon.
―Good to see you, hyung.
“It’s been a while since we last met. Can’t you say it out loud now?”
―I don’t want to.

Lee Gilyoung and Shin Yoosung began a strange battle of nerves the moment they met. Lee Gilyoung’s hair moved restlessly, almost like antennae, while Shin Yoosung’s fine body hair kept bristling as she guarded against him.
“Ajusshi, that boy keeps glaring at me.”
“Hyung, who is she?”
Apparently, their own kind really did recognize each other.
One was a monster master, and the other a bug······ master.
I wondered if the two would get along.
I asked Lee Gilyoung.
“You haven’t found Heewon-ssi yet?”
“No. But I think I know where she is. I sent bugs out to look, and Heewon-noona is up north right now.”
That was Lee Gilyoung for you. It seemed he had already looked for the others without being asked.
Come to think of it, the north was where the ‘King of Wanderers’ resided.
Perhaps Jung Heewon had made contact with that group.
“I knew you were coming too, hyung. I’d sent out lots of diving beetles.”

Now that he mentioned it, there were more bugs on Lee Gilyoung’s head. I was sure there had only been cockroaches before······. Shin Yoosung frowned as though disgusted. After checking the group’s combat strength, I came to a conclusion.

“It would be best to stay here for the remaining two days. Raise your skill proficiency as much as possible, and collect coins whenever you have spare time. Raise all your overall stats as far as you can too. Oh, and······ Yoo Sangah-ssi.”
“Yes?”
“Have you contacted your family?”
At the word ‘family,’ Yoo Sangah’s expression abruptly darkened.
As I had expected, it seemed she hadn’t been able to contact them yet.
“Donghoon.”
Han Donghoon, wearing his headphones, nodded without a word.
Han Donghoon had the skill [Wide-area Internet]. In other words, he could communicate with the outside.
Bzzzz.

Yoo Sangah’s little smartphone buzzed, and a message appeared saying it was connected to the internet. She stared down at it for a long time as though she couldn’t believe her eyes, then looked at me on the verge of tears.
I nodded and spoke.
“Tell your family about the situation here too. Once this scenario ends, the outskirts of Seoul will no longer be a safe zone either.”
“······What’s going to happen?”
“We don’t know what will happen or when, so make sure you tell them to prepare. That will be enough for now.”
“Don’t you need to contact your family, Dokja-ssi?”
“I’m all right.”
“My family is in Seoul.”
“In Seoul? Then······.”
“That person is safe.”
I silently looked north.
Then a system message rang out as though it had been waiting.
[Someone has defeated the ‘Disaster of Water’ in the north.]
It seemed the ‘King of Wanderers’ had finished the job safely too.
Now only the last one remained.
The ‘Disaster of Floods.’

「Dazzling sword light embroidered the air with a crackling sound. Dozens of sword strikes collided in an instant. The blood shadow (血影) blazing in Jung Heewon’s eyes spread through the air, scattering a ghostly aura. At last, Jung Heewon’s sword stopped.
“I think that’s enough training.”
Jung Heewon carefully inspected her blade and smiled in satisfaction. The middle-aged woman opposite her smiled faintly too.
“Jeon Woochi’s Taoist arts really are incredible.”
“Your Kendo was excellent too, Heewon-ssi. You’ll soon have a constellation sponsor as well, so I may be no match for you then.”
“You’re too kind.”

Jung Heewon quietly looked at the woman’s sky-blue prison uniform. For the past week, she had been in these people’s care. It was probably a debt she couldn’t easily repay even with all the time she had left. The middle-aged woman asked.
“Are you sure you have no intention of traveling with our <Nouvelle Vague>? Our king would be delighted to have you with us too, Heewon-ssi.”
“I’m sorry, but I have companions I’m waiting for.”
Jung Heewon clasped her hands as though genuinely sorry. The middle-aged woman gave a regretful smile of resignation. She already knew who Jung Heewon’s companions were.
“I hope that person knows how desperately you’re trying, Heewon-ssi.”
“He’ll know.”
Jung Heewon looked up at the sky with a slightly displeased expression and spoke.
“Somehow, I feel like he’s watching right now.”」
······At this rate, I couldn’t tell who had [Omniscient Reader’s Viewpoint].
Anyway, Jung Heewon seemed to be growing steadily too.
I had been worried because she was a character who never got to shine in the original novel, so I was glad it seemed my choice was proving to be right.
Next, I used [Omniscient Reader’s Viewpoint] to search for someone else’s viewpoint.
Unfortunately, only a few viewpoints were visible.
······Hmm? What was this?
A moment later, the screen rippled, and a familiar face appeared.
······Wasn’t that me?
Wait. These two?
「“Hey, you.”
Lee Gilyoung spoke in a fierce voice.
“Get away from hyung while I’m asking nicely.”
Then Shin Yoosung, pressed close beside my sleeping body, spoke.
“Don’t want to.”
“Where does a mutt like you get off······.”
“Don’t talk to me, you little bug bastard.”
Lee Gilyoung faltered. The cockroach and diving beetle on his head waved their antennae fiercely. Barely recovering his composure, Lee Gilyoung struck back.
“Hyung doesn’t like kids like you.”
“I know who ajusshi likes too.”
“······You know who hyung likes? Who?”
“Some unnie.”
Lee Gilyoung snickered.
“An unnie? I think you’ve got something wrong. Dokja-hyung likes men.”
“How would you know?”
“I know because I’ve been with hyung for a long time.”」
Just as some horrifying conversation was about to begin, I barely managed to wake up.
I hurriedly looked around, but Shin Yoosung and Lee Gilyoung were fast asleep, their heads resting against each other.
······Had I been seeing things? Was it just a dream?
“Dokja-ssi, is something wrong?”
I gave a small shake of my head at the question from Yoo Sangah, who was keeping watch.
It must have been a dream after all.
But as I lay back down, I heard whispering from somewhere.
‘Hey, bug. Come to think of it, you were in ajusshi’s arms earlier, weren’t you?’
‘Are you a baby? Ajusshi likes people who act grown-up, you know?’
Apparently, it hadn’t been a dream after all.
“You two over there······ Aren’t you going to sleep?”
Yoo Sangah’s voice. Then everything went quiet again, and soon I began to hear the children snoring.
The two days passed in a flash.
[‘Sub-scenario ― Survival Activities’ has ended.]
On hearing the system message, everyone got up and finished preparing.
A scenario that could be called long, or short.
Bihyung’s message flashed in the air.
A number out of nowhere. Bihyung spoke again.
‘What’s that?’
[What do you think? 9611.]
I immediately realized what the numbers meant.
Right. I had made a promise about ‘10,000’ back then.
[Constellations fond of the Korean Peninsula grow nervous about the number of subscribing constellations.]
I asked Bihyung.
‘You did what I told you, right?’
[······I did, but I don’t know if it’ll work. Anyway, good luck. 9781.]
Wooooo.

The huge meteorite split open in its entirety, revealing an interior reminiscent of a womb (胎內). Inside, a naked woman lay curled up, embedded like a fossil.
A woman whose snow-white skin bore a mysterious sheen.
Her beautiful hair, tied in a ponytail, enveloped her entire body.
That was what Shin Yoosung looked like as an adult.
“A woman?”
“What the hell? That's the disaster?”

Apparently Lee Hyunsung and Lee Jihye hadn't managed to stop everyone. Several incarnations who had sneaked closer were looking at her. The disparity in fighting strength seemed so vast that they couldn't sense her power.
[The exclusive skill, ‘Fourth Wall,’ offsets your mental shock.]
The ‘Disaster of Floods’ was different from the other disasters.
Unlike the other disasters, which at least suffered a weakening penalty if they hatched early, the ‘Disaster of Floods’ had no such penalty.
The earlier the Disaster of Floods woke, the stronger she became.
The moment Shin Yoosung opened her eyes, something like snow-white fur grew all over her body.
The pure white fur, reminiscent of an animal pelt, soon covered her entire body and transformed into clothing.
Creak.
Shin Yoosung slowly emerged from the meteorite and set foot on the ground. Her steps were like those of a little child learning to walk for the first time,
She had merely taken a step, yet everyone around her froze.
A powerhouse of a different species (種).
Even Lee Seolhwa, who ranked among the stronger incarnations, had gone rigid. But there was also someone utterly undaunted by Shin Yoosung's aura.
“I've been waiting, Shin Yoosung.”
Shin Yoosung slowly turned her head toward the man.
“······Captain?”
Just from that single encounter, Shin Yoosung seemed to have realized something.
“I see······ If you were waiting for me, Captain······, then this isn't the first time you've seen me. Right?”
Yoo Joonghyuk nodded.
“I need your help.”
“Before that······ Captain, what round are you on now?”
“Why do you want to know?”
“Because I need to.”
After a moment's hesitation, Yoo Joonghyuk answered.
“The 3rd round.”
“Just as I thought······. Then you met me in the 2nd round too. Right?”
“Yes.”
The reason the 2nd-round Yoo Joonghyuk had made it all the way to Scenario 46.
It was thanks to the ‘Disaster of Floods’ right before us.
Shin Yoosung, the Disaster of Floods, was someone who had come from the 41st-round worldline.
A safeguard the 41st-round Yoo Joonghyuk had sent to his past self.
After being abandoned in her own worldline, Shin Yoosung had traveled across dimensions for many years, finally descending into Earth's scenarios in the past.
“If this is the 3rd round, that means you failed even after I gave you information in the last round?”
“That's why I need more information.”
In the 2nd round, Shin Yoosung gives Yoo Joonghyuk the information she knows and chooses to take her own life. As a final kindness to the Yoo Joonghyuk she had known.
That was how it happened in the 2nd round, at any rate.
Shin Yoosung spoke.
“······It took thousands of years.”
In Shin Yoosung's expressionless face, I could feel a weariness spanning unfathomable ages.
What the 41st-round Yoo Joonghyuk had done was more terrible than murder.
Thousands of years. Enough time for a personality to collapse entirely and a sense of self to wear away.
Shin Yoosung had endured that time and finally become a ‘disaster.’
“Captain, do you know? How much I suffered. How many agonizing years I endured to carry out your request.”
“······What are you talking about?”
“I'm saying I missed you terribly, Captain.”
Yoo Joonghyuk completely failed to understand the despair in Shin Yoosung's bright smile. He spoke in an indifferent tone.
“Give me all the information from the 41st round. Did the version of me from that round say anything else?”
I wanted to shout that he shouldn't say that.
But I couldn't make a sound.
Shin Yoosung's gaze was as calm as the eye of a storm.
Only I could read the emotions raging in the depths of those eyes.
「So nothing changes after all.」
Because of Yoo Joonghyuk's plan, Shin Yoosung had wandered alone through the labyrinth of worldlines for more than a thousand years.
For two hundred years, she had endured for humanity. For another two hundred, she had endured on the strength of a promise to protect the world.
And for another two hundred years, she had endured by thinking of Yoo Joonghyuk and the companions who had been with her.
Through those long years, Shin Yoosung had revisited a handful of memories, over and over, to preserve herself.
But the more she ruminated on them, the more a certain question rose within her.
「What does any of this mean?」
Time erased her greater cause and robbed her of justice.
Where the greater cause had vanished, all that remained was a pitiful human truth.
Resentment toward Yoo Joonghyuk, who had reduced her and her companions to mere tools for ‘regression.’
Amid loneliness that seeped into her bones and the desolation of losing her world, Shin Yoosung endured for a thousand years while hating Yoo Joonghyuk, who had made her this way.
“You never change, Captain, no matter when I see you.”
“Stop wasting words and give me the information first. There's no time.”
“What were ‘we’ to you, Captain?”
“I did my duty. I gave you one chance, too. But you're still the same.”
As a final act of mercy, she had helped the 2nd-round Yoo Joonghyuk.

“And you'll keep being the same. You'll use people like tools again, and throw me into that horrific labyrinth of worldlines. That paltry sense of justice, that damned greater cause. I hate you for living in this world as though you're alone.”
And now, she had come face-to-face with the 3rd-round Yoo Joonghyuk.
“So there's only one thing I'll tell you. You can't save anyone, Captain.”
Shin Yoosung smiled chillingly.
“Your 3rd round ends here.”

Dazzling light shimmered in Shin Yoosung's hand at almost the exact moment I released the pressure-point seal. I sprinted with all my strength and intercepted the ether storm exploding before my eyes.
“Move, Yoo Joonghyuk!”

Pain erupted as though my entire lower abdomen were being ripped away, and for a moment my mind went blank. A massive crater formed in the center of the island. Yoo Joonghyuk and I were thrown into the air and rolled across the ground for a long while.
It hurts. Damn it. It really hurts.
“······Kim Dokja?”
A startled Yoo Joonghyuk looked down at me where I lay.
My breathing grew labored, and the sky turned yellow.
It hits me just how lucky I've been until now.
This was the kind of world it had always been.
A world where one tiny misstep could leave you fucking dead.
“Kim Dokja!”
What a fuss this bastard was making.
I grinned and spoke to Yoo Joonghyuk.
“Hey, kill me, will you? You've always wanted to kill me so badly.”
“······What are you talking about?”
“I'll give you just 1 minute to kill me, so kill me.”

Only then did Yoo Joonghyuk look at my lower abdomen. So this is what it feels like to want to touch your stomach when there's no stomach left. Bloody foam kept spilling from my mouth, and the whole world spun so badly I felt like throwing up. Hic,
and my breath keeps catching.

“Hold on, Kim Dokja! It's not too late.”

“It's not too late!”

It had been a very long time since I'd seen that expression on Yoo Joonghyuk's face.
The bastard had worn that same expression when he first saw me on the subway.
“I can't do that.”
My vision blurred.

I could see Yoo Joonghyuk pressing my pressure points, but I'd already lost too much blood. And above all······ there was no way I could live with the lower part of my entrails gone. Even Lee Seolhwa couldn't handle this.

In the darkness, I heard a message I had heard once before.

Third-Person Observer's Viewpoint.
「“Flood forth.”」

The intermediate dokkaebi had been right to say that all the other disasters combined fell short of the Disaster of Floods alone. At that single utterance from Shin Yoosung, space distorted and monsters came spilling out.
[Monster Gate], the signature ability of the Legend-grade attribute [Beast Lord].
Countless monsters she had tamed during her travels across dimensions were being unleashed upon Earth as nightmares.
「“Tear, shatter, and destroy.”」
Besides grade-7 monsters, there were considerable numbers of monsters of grade 6 and above. Some were even comparable to grade-5 fire dragons, which were called minor disasters.
「“Now is the time of disaster.”」
Nodeul Island exploded, and the entire Han River became a single wave.

The panicking incarnations became food for the monsters amid their screams. I could see the ‘kings,’ who had belatedly organized their forces, issuing orders. Just then, I spotted someone radiating a terrifying aura behind Shin Yoosung.
「“I will kill you, Shin Yoosung.”」
······Had that bastard lost his mind?
With a fearsome tearing hiss, Yoo Joonghyuk's Ether Blade slashed through the air.
Shin Yoosung easily bent at the waist to evade the attack, then smiled.
「“Your ‘Breaking the Sky Swordsmanship’ level is already pretty high, isn't it? But no matter how much you lash out, you can't beat me with that. It's only at the ‘level’ stage, isn't it?”

“I will definitely kill you.”

I quietly prepared [First-Person Protagonist's Viewpoint].
In this situation, immersing myself in Yoo Joonghyuk would probably be best.

「“Something's strange······ Are you really the Captain I knew?”」
That was when Shin Yoosung, who had been tilting her head, turned her gaze toward my dead body.
「“Who's that man? There was no one like him in the round I knew.”」
Yoo Joonghyuk still said nothing.
Instead, he swung his sword, swung it, and swung it again.
As though that alone was the only answer he could give.
And how long had he been swinging it?

Shin Yoosung's face gradually filled with distrust and suspicion.
